characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SmartLab SE, Rigaku, Japan; Cu Kα radiation, working voltage 40 kV, current 40 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: Sample 1 is labelled Fe-Cr; the main phase is the Fe-Cr phase with diffraction peaks indexed (1 1 0)/(100), (2 0 0)/(200) and (2 1 1)/(211); the (1 1 0) peak lies just below 45° and is shifted to higher 2θ relative to standard Fe, indicating lattice distortion from Cr/Ni substitution.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Microhardness indenter HVS-1000A, Laizhou Huayin Testing Instrument Co., Ltd., China
characterization_methods.key_findings: Experimental microhardness of Sample 1 = 515 HV (predicted 521 HV, error 1.17%); attributed to the solid solution phases.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers microhardness of the coatings

analytical_models.equation_role: ΔσSSS = Z · M · G · δEc · DEc (predicts solid solution strengthening strength)
analytical_models.model_note: Z is a fitting parameter with a value of 0.0056; M is the Taylor factor with a value of 3.06 for both FCC and BCC structures. G is the shear modulus; δEc is the difference in cohesive energy and DEc is the local cohesive energy mismatch.

parameters.name: M (Taylor factor, both FCC and BCC)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Key input features {G, δEc, DEc}; output = microhardness (HV). SVR hyperparameters: C = 4.98, cache_size = 118.85, coef0 = 0.63, degree = 4, epsilon = 1.87 × 10⁻⁴, gamma = 3.57 × 10⁻², kernel = poly, tol = 1.22 × 10⁻³.
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Training data obtained from MatWeb (173 Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel data points, augmented from 98 to 192 by conditional generative adversarial networks, CGANs); 117 MatWeb data points used as independent validation set
computational_details.simulation_method: Machine learning support vector regression (SVR) model combined with modified solid solution strengthening theory; hyperparameters optimized with Bayesian optimization and ten-fold cross-validation; the inverse design used firefly optimization algorithm (FA) to determine element content
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For Sample 1 the model predicted a microhardness of 521 HV versus the experimental 515 HV (error 1.17%). With the modified solid solution strengthening theory the SVR model achieved R² = 0.89 and RMSE = 0.31 (R² increased by 4.71% and RMSE decreased by 8.34% relative to the model without the modified theory).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Error between predicted and experimental microhardness: Sample 1 = 1.17%, which is lower than the 2.01% and 2.96% errors previously reported for predicting the hardness of high entropy alloys (Ren et al. [14] and Huang et al. [47]).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The wire with the optimized element content (Sample 1 composition) was used as the feeding material. ASTM A36 steel plates of 300 mm × 120 mm × 40 mm were used as substrates. Arc cladding equipment IDEALARC DC-1000 (Lincoln Electric, America) was used to prepare the Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si coatings. Cladding parameters: current 440 ~ 600 A, voltage 30 ~ 32 V, cladding speed 24 m/h, interlayer temperature 380 ~ 410 °C, wire feed speed 76.8 m/h.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with a microhardness indenter (HVS-1000A, Laizhou Huayin Testing Instrument Co., Ltd., China); load 1 kg with holding time of 20 s.

aliases: Sample 1 of the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys

defects.lattice_distortion: The diffraction peak of the alloy was shifted to the right (higher 2θ) relative to the standard Fe diffraction peak, due to the atomic radius differences between Cr, Ni and Fe, resulting in lattice distortion.

phases_present.morphology: solid solution; Cr atoms randomly substitute Fe atoms in the FCC lattice

structures.overall_structure: Sample 1 (Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si coating) is composed mainly of the Fe-Cr phase; the Cr atoms randomly substitute Fe atoms in the FCC lattice, forming a solid-solution main phase, with the diffraction peaks of 100, 200 and 211.

unmapped_findings: Sample 1 composition (mass %) from Table 6: C 0.45, Si 0.19, Mn 1.53, Cr 14, S 0.01, Ni 0, P 0.014, Fe 83.806, Mo 0, V 0, W 0. Derived parameters: δr = 0.0542 and ΔHmix = −0.914 kJ/mol.
Sample 1 is described as one of the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys designed by the ML model and fabricated by arc cladding for experimental validation.
The ML model predicted a microhardness of 521 HV for Sample 1 versus a measured 515 HV, giving the minimum error of 1.17% among the three samples.

Solid-solution formation criterion for the designed samples: solid solution phases form when δr < 0.066 and −11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol; the samples' δ values range 0.0335 to 0.0595 and ΔHmix ranges −1.213 to −0.451 kJ/mol, satisfying the criterion.

There is a labeling discrepancy for Sample 1's phase: the Results text calls the main phase the Fe-Cr phase with an FCC lattice and peaks 100/200/211, whereas Fig. 8 labels it Fe-Cr with reflections indexed (1 1 0)/(2 0 0)/(2 1 1) and describes a bcc-type solid-solution phase.
